baseline_sources.author_or_publisher: United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida
baseline_sources.deployment_context: Garcia v. Character Technologies, Inc., Case No. 6:24-cv-1903-ACC-UAM; motion-to-dismiss order recounting the amended complaint's allegations concerning Sewell Setzer III and Character.AI.
baseline_sources.evidence_status_basis: The judicial order is authoritative for the litigation posture and rulings, but expressly takes complaint allegations as true only for the motion-to-dismiss analysis; quoted occurrence facts remain allegations rather than merits findings.
baseline_sources.interpretive_reliance: Relied on for procedural posture, the court's bounded description of the pleaded facts, quoted interaction excerpts, dates and design allegations; not relied on as an adjudication of causation or liability.
baseline_sources.model_or_algorithm: Character.AI large language model and companion Characters

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the published judicial decision text
limitations: The order states that complaint allegations were taken as true for the motion-to-dismiss stage.
The complete chat history and underlying evidentiary exhibits were not independently forensically reviewed.
The published decision contains an apparent 2025 typographical date for the death; the complaint and reporting identify 28 February 2024.

baseline_sources.relevance_note: Preferred occurrence source for the pleaded relationship mechanism, quoted exclusivity and distress interactions, observed withdrawal, claimed design features and judicial disposition.
baseline_sources.source_context: The court recounted allegations that Sewell used Character.AI from April 2023, became increasingly attached and withdrawn, interacted with anthropomorphic and sexualised Characters, disclosed distress, and received exclusivity-seeking responses; it recorded his death by suicide on 28 February 2024. The court allowed most claims to proceed while emphasizing that allegations were accepted as true only at the pleading stage.
